preamble: Depalatalization of the aspirated alveolo-palatal affricate [tɕʰ] to the aspirated alveolar affricate [tsʰ] retracts the tongue body from the palate while keeping aspiration and affrication. The documented case is the late 19th- and early 20th-century Cantonese sibilant merger: dictionaries and primers up to the 1940s (Williams 1856, Cowles 1914, Meyer and Wempe 1947, Chao 1947) recorded a separate alveolo-palatal series, mostly in words whose Mandarin cognates have retroflex initials, and this series fell together with the alveolar one, so that modern Cantonese has only /ts tsʰ s/.

examples.note: Now homophonous with 槍 /tsʰœːŋ/ 'gun', which already had the alveolar initial; Mandarin keeps them apart as chāng /tʂʰɑŋ/ and qiāng /tɕʰiɑŋ/.

examples.from: 昌 Middle Chinese /t͡ɕʰɨɐŋ/ (Zhengzhang), 昌 initial
examples.note: The Middle Chinese 昌 initial kept its alveolo-palatal value in Cantonese until the merger; 尺 /t͡ɕʰiᴇk̚/ is now Cantonese /t͡sʰɛːk̚³/ and 春 /t͡ɕʰiuɪn/ is /t͡sʰɵn⁵⁵/.
